paper.title: SLTUNET: A Simple Unified Model for Sign Language Translation
paper.citation: Biao Zhang, Mathias Müller, and Rico Sennrich. SLTUNET: A Simple Unified Model for Sign Language Translation. In The Eleventh International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR), 2023.

sources.role: Target and protocol source. The assignment pointed at the OpenReview PDF, but openreview.net served an HTTP 403 bot challenge to both the fetch tool and curl on 2026-09-13, so the arXiv v1 copy of the same ICLR 2023 camera-ready was hashed instead. The arXiv copy carries the 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023' header and the same tables; the OpenReview record remains the canonical citation.

The authors' official implementation, linked from the paper abstract. Contains the SLTUNET model, the adapted SMKD sign-embedding pretraining code under smkd/, the evaluation metrics under eval/, the PHOENIX walk-through under example/, and the DGS3-T construction scripts under dgs3-t/. Master branch, latest commit dated 2023-07-10.

Authors' released trained models for PHOENIX and CSL-Daily (phoenix.tar.gz, csldaily.tar.gz, csldaily2.tar.gz, dgs3-t.tar.gz), announced in the repository README on 2023-07-09. Directory listing confirmed reachable on 2026-09-13 but no archive has been downloaded or hashed yet, so this source is not pinned. Intended use is an evaluation-path preflight and a check of the decoding/metric pipeline before any training run; a score obtained from the authors' own weights verifies the artifact and is not by itself a reproduction of their training.

Upstream SMKD/VAC_CSLR implementation cited by the paper (footnote 1) as the sign embedding extractor. The sltunet repository vendors an adapted copy under smkd/, so the vendored copy pinned through published-code is the artifact that will actually run; this upstream is recorded because the paper cites it and because the paper reports retraining SMKD with a 2D ResNet34 backbone.

datasets.precomputed_features_note: The volume also holds features/phoenix14t.pami0.{train,dev,test}, which are the Camgoz et al. (2020b) sign embeddings. These are NOT the embeddings behind the target numbers: Table 2 row 1.1 shows that using Camgoz et al. (2020b) embeddings scores 21.21 B@4 on dev, whereas the SLTUNET result requires the authors' retrained SMKD embeddings with a 2D ResNet34 backbone (18.90 WER, row 15, 27.87 B@4). Reproducing the targets therefore requires SMKD pretraining from the videos in videos/, not reuse of these features. Using them instead would be a behaviour-changing protocol deviation and would reproduce a different table row.

datasets.verification_note: Verified 2026-09-13: the shared Volume already contains 'dgs-corpus/' with videos/, dgs.json, download.py, index.py, and split.3.0.0-uzh-document.json. That split file is the DGS3-T protocol itself: it declares dgs_corpus_version '3.0.0' and partitions documents 384 train / 10 dev / 10 test, matching Appendix A.2, which states the desired number of documents in dev and test is 10 each. 'uzh' matches the authors' institution (Müller and Sennrich, University of Zurich). Availability is therefore no longer the obstacle; permission is. Only the split manifest was read, to establish gate status. No corpus content was processed. sha256 of the split manifest: a687622057adc8f7b2423ab457280dd1a37b0db3906bb42a4b112a5739cd5378.

experiments.system: SLTUNET, final configuration (system 15 of Table 2): d=256, h=4, dff=4096, N^P_enc=1, N^S_enc=5, N_dec=6, CTC alpha=0.3, stochastic BPE dropout (rate 0.2, stochastic rate 0.6), Xavier gain 0.5, sign-frame random crop and horizontal flip, trained on the Equation 4 multi-task objective with MT data, using sign embeddings from the retrained SMKD model with a 2D ResNet34 backbone. Evaluated end-to-end (Sign2Text).
experiments.checkpoint_rule: Average of the best 10 checkpoints ranked by dev-set Sign2Text performance, then beam search with beam size 8 and a length penalty tuned on the dev set (paper Appendix A.1; repository checkpoint_averaging.py and example/test.sh).

gates.reason: The DGS3-T data and the authors' exact split are already present in the study's shared approved Volume as 'dgs-corpus/', including split.3.0.0-uzh-document.json (version 3.0.0, 384/10/10 documents, matching Appendix A.2 and bearing the authors' institution tag). Availability is therefore not the obstacle. The Public DGS Corpus licence still forbids computational research without express permission from the University of Hamburg, and this attempt has no record of whether the study holds such permission, what it covers, or whether it extends to training models and publishing translation outputs. Proceeding on the assumption that presence implies permission would be working around a restriction.

Note the corpus contains identifiable video of 330 named signers, so the reporting and retention terms attached to any permission need reading too.

gates.reason: The targets require sign embeddings from the authors' retrained SMKD model with a 2D ResNet34 backbone, which must be pretrained from video per benchmark. The precomputed features already in the PHOENIX volume are the Camgoz et al. (2020b) embeddings, which the paper's own Table 2 row 1.1 shows produce a materially different score (21.21 versus 22.62 B@4 for the baseline, and the final SLTUNET number depends on the improved SMKD model). Substituting them would reproduce a different row. SMKD pretraining from video is the dominant cost in this reproduction and has not been estimated, because no preflight has run.
gates.required_action: Measure SMKD pretraining cost on a representative preflight once the environment exists, then apply the compute gate: proceed autonomously if the whole plan is single-GPU and under 24 hours, otherwise discuss in #repro-sign-team-r before launching. The estimate must cover SMKD pretraining plus SLTUNET training for both PHOENIX-2014T and CSL-Daily.
evidence: Paper section 5.1: the SMKD model is pretrained on each benchmark separately on the Sign2Gloss task.
Paper section 5.2: replacing Camgoz et al. (2020b) embeddings with the retrained SMKD model gives +1.41 BLEU, and the ResNet34 backbone change gives a further +0.31 BLEU into the final system 15.
Wrapper listing on 2026-09-13: the volume's PHOENIX features are phoenix14t.pami0.*, the Camgoz et al. (2020b) embeddings.
Repository example/README.md step 2 describes SMKD pretraining, checkpoint averaging, and feature extraction with --num-feature-aug 10 as prerequisites of SLTUNET training.

environment_plan.published_requirements: python==3.8, tensorflow==1.15 (repository README 'Requirement'); no requirements.txt or lockfile is published.
environment_plan.base_image_conflict: The repository's standard GPU base image ghcr.io/sign-language-processing/reproduction:latest supplies NVIDIA NGC PyTorch. SLTUNET is TensorFlow 1.15, which needs CUDA 10.0 / cuDNN 7.x and will not run on that image, so a paper-specific Dockerfile is expected. This is an environment adaptation, not a change to the published code, and the exact image has not been chosen or built yet.
environment_plan.video_decoding: The published SLTUNET training path consumes precomputed SMKD sign features in .h5 files rather than decoding video, so no video decoder is introduced for it. The upstream SMKD feature-extraction step does read frames and is where simple-video-utils would apply if that step is rerun.
environment_plan.planned_first_check: An evaluation-path preflight using the authors' released PHOENIX checkpoint, to exercise decoding, checkpoint averaging, and eval/metrics.py against the published Table 4 numbers before committing to SMKD pretraining plus full SLTUNET training.

open_questions: Whether the study wants the DGS3-T targets pursued at all, given that permission from the University of Hamburg is a prerequisite and may not be obtainable within the study.

Whether reproducing Table 4/5 requires retraining SMKD sign embeddings from video (the expensive path the paper describes) or whether the authors' released checkpoints and any released features make a shorter path defensible; this changes the compute estimate by a large factor and has not been costed.
